chunks: Their argument based on what has been narrated that the Master of this Affair will live after he dies and that he was named Qaim because he will rise after he dies,

is invalid, because that, if the report were reliable, could be interpreted to mean that he will rise after his name dies, so that no one mentions him except those who believe in his Imamate, and then Allah will manifest him to all the creation.
Besides, we have established that every Imam who stands in place of the previous Imam is called the Qaim.

key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْأَمْرِ: Master of the Affair (a title for the Imam)
key_terms.قَائِمًا: The Riser / The One who stands up

ai.seo_question: What is the theological meaning of the title 'Al-Qaim' in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Al-Tusi refutes the claim that the title 'Al-Qaim' necessitates a physical rising after death by proposing an alternative interpretation: the Imam's memory or recognition may cease before he reappears, at which point God restores his visibility to all. He further contextualizes this by noting that 'Qaim' is a generic title for any Imam who rises to succeed his predecessor, thereby preventing sects from monopolizing the term for the Mahdi alone.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: The argument, which is based on the tradition that “the Master of this Affair will live after he dies” and that he has been named Qaim, since he will rise after he dies, is invalid, because first the tradition is not reliable, and even if it is reliable, it can be interpreted to mean that he will rise after his name dies, that is, no one mentions him, except those who believe in his Imamate and then Allah will manifest him to all.
Besides, we have established that every Imam, who stands in place of a previous Imam, is called the Qaim.
